elements.quote: A systematic review and meta-analysis were performed using randomized clinical trials and observational studies.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review (and meta-analysis).

elements.quote: The aim of this review is to compare a removable orthosis versus a cast regarding safety and functional outcome in the NOM of stable type B ankle fractures.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective/review question explicitly.
The abstract does not state the main inclusion or exclusion criteria; eligibility details appear only in the Methods (text_6).
The abstract does not mention information sources (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane) or the last search date; these appear only in the Methods.

elements.quote: The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed with the methodological index for non-randomized studies instrument.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the risk-of-bias/methodological quality assessment method (MINORS).

elements.quote: Nonoperative management was compared using the number of complications and functional outcome measured using the Olerud and Molander Score (OMAS) or the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons Ankle Score.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates meta-analysis was performed and describes how results were compared and synthesized (complications, OMAS/AAOS scores).

elements.quote: Five studies were included. Two were randomized clinical trials, and three were observational studies, including a total of 516 patients.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies, participants, and relevant study characteristics (designs).

elements.quote: A meta-analysis showed statistically significant higher odds of developing complications in the cast group [odds ratio (OR), 4.67 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.52-14.35)]. Functional outcome in OMAS did not vary significantly at 6 weeks, mean difference (MD) - 6.64 (95% CI - 13.72 to + 0.45), and at 12 weeks, MD - 6.91 (95% CI - 18.73 to + 4.91).
elements.reason: The abstract presents quantitative results for the main outcomes (complications and functional outcome at multiple time points).

elements.quote: odds ratio (OR), 4.67 (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.52-14.35)
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the abstract reports summary estimates with 95% confidence intervals.

elements.quote: The mean difference of functional outcome in OMAS at 26 weeks or longer was significantly better in the removable orthosis group; MD - 2.63 (95% CI - 5.01 to - 0.25).
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect and which group is favored (removable orthosis favored at 26 weeks; cast group had higher complication odds).
The abstract does not mention limitations of the included evidence such as risk of bias, inconsistency, or imprecision.

elements.quote: Results of this systematic review and meta-analysis show that a removable orthosis is a safe alternative type of NOM, as complication numbers are significantly lower in the orthosis group.
elements.reason: The Conclusion section of the abstract provides a general interpretation and implications of the results.
The abstract does not state the funding source for the review.
The abstract provides no registration name or number; the Methods note no published protocol exists, and no registration is reported.

elements.quote: Removable orthoses have proven their value in the recovery process of other fractures of the long bones, and are increasingly suggested as an alternative to a cast for stable type B fractures [16, 17]. ... Both types of NOM have benefits and drawbacks, but no consensus on NOM for stable type B ankle fractures has been reached.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the current state of knowledge (orthoses proven for other long-bone fractures and increasingly suggested for stable type B fractures) and the key uncertainty (no consensus on nonoperative management, also stated in the abstract: 'There is currently no consensus on nonoperative management in adult patients after a stable type B ankle fracture'). Note: these rationale sentences appear in a retrieved chunk whose section label is 'Assessment Of Methodological Quality' but whose content is clearly Introduction-style text.

elements.quote: Both types of NOM have benefits and drawbacks, but no consensus on NOM for stable type B ankle fractures has been reached. The aim of this review was to compare a removable orthosis versus a cast regarding safety and functional outcome in the NOM of stable type B ankle fractures.
elements.reason: The need for the review is explained by the identified gap (both treatment options have benefits and drawbacks but no consensus exists) and a clearly stated review aim addressing that gap. Clinical importance is conveyed by the context that orthoses are 'increasingly suggested as an alternative' and may prevent 'the consequences of rigid immobilization and accelerating recovery.'

elements.quote: To our knowledge, this is the first literature overview that compares NOM for stable type B ankle fractures.
elements.reason: The authors explicitly state this is the first literature overview comparing nonoperative management (cast vs orthosis) for stable type B ankle fractures. No similar systematic review is identified or cited as being updated or replicated; the only related prior work mentioned is 'a recent appraisal of a published study' with a broader fracture range, which is not clearly identified as a systematic review. The conditional requirement to justify the review relative to existing similar reviews therefore does not apply on the basis of the reported evidence.

elements.quote: Orthoses can be taken off, allowing early (weight-bearing) mobilization, potentially preventing the consequences of rigid immobilization and accelerating recovery [16, 18].
elements.reason: This is a review of intervention effects (cast vs removable orthosis), and the proposed mechanism of action of the removable orthosis is briefly described: removability enables early weight-bearing mobilization, avoiding the consequences of rigid immobilization and accelerating recovery.

The review compares two simple, single-component immobilization modalities (cast versus removable orthosis) for one fracture type; it does not evaluate a complex, multi-component intervention or a complex delivery context, so a logic model showing relationships between intervention components and outcomes is not required and none is presented.

elements.quote: The aim of this review is to compare a removable orthosis versus a cast regarding safety and functional outcome in the NOM of stable type B ankle fractures.
elements.reason: An explicit objective statement is given in the abstract (Purpose) and repeated in the introduction (text_4), clearly defining the review question comparing removable orthosis versus cast for safety and functional outcome.

elements.quote: Studies were included if: (1) NOM with a cast versus removable orthosis after stable type B ankle fractures were compared, (2) included patients were skeletally mature (16 years or older), (3) complications (e.g. DVT, stiffness) and functional outcome measured in Patient Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) up to 52 weeks were described
elements.reason: The planned comparison (cast vs removable orthosis), population (skeletally mature adults with stable type B ankle fractures), and outcomes (complications, functional outcome) are identifiable from eligibility criteria and the objective, but the comparison is not formally framed using PICO or an explicitly structured variant.

elements.quote: Studies were included if: (1) NOM with a cast versus removable orthosis after stable type B ankle fractures were compared, (2) included patients were skeletally mature (16 years or older), (3) complications (e.g. DVT, stiffness) and functional outcome measured in Patient Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) up to 52 weeks were described
elements.reason: Eligibility criteria specify population (skeletally mature, stable type B ankle fractures), intervention/comparison (cast vs removable orthosis), outcomes (complications and PROMs), and follow-up requirement (up to 52 weeks).

elements.quote: (4) available in Dutch, English, or German, (5) original data was reported (no reviews, editorial letters, or expert opinions)
elements.reason: Language and publication/report status criteria are specified, but no dissemination year restriction is reported.
No evidence distinguishes exclusion of studies because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: NOM with a cast versus removable orthosis after stable type B ankle fractures were compared
elements.reason: The synthesis groups (cast vs removable orthosis) are defined and directly linked to the review's stated aim of comparing removable orthosis versus cast for safety and functional outcome (text_4).
Restrictions such as the language limitation and the 16-years-or-older requirement are stated but no rationales for these notable restrictions are provided.
